 Pakistan Shaheens leave for Doha to defend Asia Cup Rising Stars title

 Pakistan Shaheens left Karachi in the early hours of Monday for Doha, Qatar, to compete in the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, scheduled to take place from November 19 to 29. 
 The 15-member squad, captained by Abdul Samad, will be joined in Doha by Ali Raza and Farhan Yousuf, who recently represented Pakistan in the ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup in Oman, a Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) statement said.
 Defending champions Pakistan have been placed in Group B alongside India ‘A’, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
 They will open their campaign against the UAE on 20 November before taking on India ‘A’ on 22 November and Nepal on 24 November.
 Speaking to PCB Digital ahead of the team’s departure, captain Abdul Samad expressed confidence in the side’s preparations and said the players were ready for the 50-over competition.
 “Our preparations have been good. We have played scenario-based matches throughout the week, while the coaching staff has worked hard with the players to prepare for the 50-over tournament. We are confident of putting up strong performances in the event,” he said.
 Samad added that the team’s immediate priority would be to secure victory in the opening fixture and build momentum for the remainder of the tournament.
 “If we execute our plans effectively, I am confident that we will achieve positive results, which will also benefit the players in future events,” he added.
 Pakistan Shaheens won the previous 50-over edition in 2023, defeating India ‘A’ by 128 runs in the final in Sri Lanka.
 They also claimed the title in the most recent edition, which was played in the T20 format, beating Bangladesh ‘A’ in a thrilling final decided by a Super Over.
 Pakistan Shaheens squad 
 Abdul Samad (captain), Ahmed Daniyal, Ali Raza, Danish Aziz, Farhan Yousuf, Haider Ali, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Hasnain, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Rohail Nazir (wicketkeeper), Saad Masood, Shahzaib Khan, Shamyl Hussain and Sufyan Moqim.
 Pakistan Shaheens’ fixtures 
 November 20: vs UAE, 11am Pakistan time– University of Doha for Science and Technology
 November 22: vs India ‘A’, 3pm – West End Park International Cricket Stadium
 November 24: vs Nepal, 3pm – West End Park International Cricket Stadium
 November 26: First semi-final, 3pm – West End Park International Cricket Stadium
 November 27: Second semi-final, 3pm – West End Park International Cricket Stadium
 November 29: Final, 3pm – West End Park International Cricket Stadium
